threeYearPlan.title: 3-Year Chess Mastery Plan
threeYearPlan.subtitle: From complete beginner to strong club player (1800-2000 rating)

year1.title: Year 1: Foundation Building
year1.description: Master the basics, tactical patterns, and fundamental endgames

months.title: Rules, Board & Notation
months.focus: Absolute basics — legal moves, notation, how each piece moves and captures

session1.details: Practice how each piece moves and captures on an empty board, then with obstacles

session2.details: Read and write algebraic notation; replay 5 short master games move-by-move

session3.details: Play 1-2 slow games (15+10 or longer) against a similarly-rated opponent, no time pressure

session4.details: Write your own game in notation and check it against an app's move list for errors

weeklyGoals: Name every square on the board instantly (files a-h, ranks 1-8)
Move every piece correctly, including castling, en passant and promotion
Recognise check, checkmate and stalemate on sight
Record a full game in algebraic notation without help
resources: Learn Chess the Right Way Vol.1 (Susan Polgar)

months.title: Basic Checkmates
months.focus: Forcing checkmate with king+queen, king+rook, and two rooks vs lone king

session1.details: Practice mating with king and queen against a lone king from 10 random positions

session2.details: Practice the 'lawnmower' technique with king and rook against a lone king

session3.details: Solve 15 mate-in-1 and mate-in-2 puzzles

session4.details: Play games starting from a material-up position and convert to checkmate

weeklyGoals: Deliver checkmate with K+Q vs K in under 10 moves, every time
Deliver checkmate with K+R vs K in under 16 moves without stalemating
Solve mate-in-1 puzzles with 95%+ accuracy
Understand why stalemate happens and how to avoid it

months.title: Core Tactics I — Fork, Pin & Skewer
months.focus: The three most common tactical weapons and how to spot them

session1.details: Study one tactical motif in depth: definition, patterns, worked examples

session2.details: Solve 15 puzzles filtered to that day's motif (fork, pin, or skewer)

session3.details: Play 2 games looking for forks/pins/skewers before every move (Checks, Captures, Threats)

session4.details: Re-solve missed puzzles and explain out loud why the tactic works

weeklyGoals: Correctly identify a fork, pin, and skewer from a diagram within 5 seconds
Solve 60+ themed puzzles this month at 80%+ accuracy
Successfully execute at least one fork or pin in a real game
Explain the difference between an absolute pin and a relative pin

months.title: Core Tactics II — Discovered & Double Attacks
months.focus: Discovered attacks, discovered checks, and double attacks

session1.details: Study discovered attacks/checks — how moving one piece unleashes another

session2.details: Solve 15 puzzles on discovered attacks and double attacks

session3.details: Play 2 games purposely setting up discovered attacks

session4.details: Review 3 of your own recent games for missed discovered attacks against you

weeklyGoals: Recognise a discovered attack setup 3 moves before it happens
Solve 60+ themed puzzles this month at 80%+ accuracy
Avoid walking into a discovered check in any practice game this month
Combine two tactical motifs (e.g., pin + fork) in at least one puzzle

months.title: Opening Principles
months.focus: Centre control, development, king safety, and the three golden rules

session1.details: Study the 3 opening principles and the top 5 beginner opening mistakes

session2.details: Replay 3 short classic games noting how they develop and castle quickly

session3.details: Play 2 games with 1.e4 or 1.d4, castling by move 10 and developing before double pawn moves

session4.details: Annotate the first 10 moves of one game, marking any principle you broke

weeklyGoals: Castle within the first 10 moves in every practice game
Avoid bringing the queen out before move 4 in every practice game
Name and explain all 3 opening principles from memory
Identify one opening mistake made by an opponent and punish it
resources: Logical Chess: Move by Move (Chernev) — first 5 games

months.title: Basic Pawn Endgames
months.focus: King and pawn endgames — opposition, the square rule, key squares

session1.details: Learn opposition and practice winning/drawing K+P vs K positions

session2.details: Learn the square rule for passed pawns and practice on the board

session3.details: Solve 15 king and pawn endgame puzzles/studies

session4.details: Play training games from a K+P vs K or K+2P vs K+P starting position

weeklyGoals: Win every winning K+P vs K position using opposition
Correctly apply the square rule to judge if a pawn can be caught
Identify key squares for a given pawn and king position
Convert an extra pawn into a win in at least one practice game
resources: 100 Endgames You Must Know (Jesus de la Villa) — ch.1

months.title: Checkmating Patterns
months.focus: Back rank mate, smothered mate, ladder mate, and other recurring mating nets

session1.details: Study one named checkmate pattern per day with 3 worked diagrams

session2.details: Solve 15 puzzles on that day's mating pattern

session3.details: Play 2 games trying to force checkmate rather than just winning material

session4.details: Do a 3-minute Puzzle Rush / Storm session focused on mate patterns

weeklyGoals: Recognise back rank mate threats and how to prevent them (luft)
Execute a smothered mate pattern at least once (puzzle or game)
Solve 60+ mate-pattern puzzles at 80%+ accuracy
Build a personal list of 5 favourite mating patterns with diagrams

months.title: Basic Strategy — Pawn Structure & Weak Squares
months.focus: Introduction to positional play: good vs bad pawns, weak squares, outposts

session1.details: Study isolated, doubled, and backward pawns; what makes a square weak

session2.details: Replay 2 annotated master games highlighting a weak-square or outpost strategy

session3.details: Play 2 games consciously trying to plant a knight on an outpost or avoid weak pawns

session4.details: Do 10 'assess the position' exercises on pawn structure

weeklyGoals: Define isolated, doubled, and backward pawns with an example of each
Identify an outpost square in a given position
Avoid creating unnecessary pawn weaknesses in 2 consecutive practice games
Use the in-app imbalance checklist to assess one full game
resources: My System (Aron Nimzowitsch) — pawn chain chapters
Silman's How to Reassess Your Chess — intro imbalances

months.title: Rook Endgames I — Lucena & Philidor
months.focus: The two most important rook endgame positions every player must know

session1.details: Study the Lucena position and the 'building a bridge' technique

session2.details: Study the Philidor position and third-rank defence

session3.details: Solve 15 rook endgame puzzles, focusing on Lucena/Philidor recognition

session4.details: Play training games from a rook + pawn vs rook starting position

weeklyGoals: Win the Lucena position from any starting square in under 10 moves
Hold the Philidor position as the defender against a rook and pawn
Recognise when a rook endgame is a theoretical draw vs a win
Explain why an active rook matters more than an extra pawn in many rook endings
resources: 100 Endgames You Must Know (Jesus de la Villa) — rook chapters

months.title: Building an Opening Repertoire
months.focus: Choosing and learning 1-2 openings for White and Black to reach playable middlegames

session1.details: Learn the main line and typical plans of your chosen White opening (e.g., Italian Game or London System)

session2.details: Learn a solid reply to 1.e4 (e.g., Caro-Kann or short French) to move 8-10

session3.details: Learn a solid reply to 1.d4 (e.g., QGD or King's Indian) to move 8-10

session4.details: Play 2 games using only your chosen repertoire, then check the moves against theory

weeklyGoals: Play your White opening from memory to move 8 without hesitation
Play your Black defence vs 1.e4 from memory to move 8
Play your Black defence vs 1.d4 from memory to move 8
Identify the typical middlegame plan (pawn break or piece manoeuvre) for each opening

months.title: Calculation & the CCT Method
months.focus: Combining tactics with structured calculation: Checks, Captures, Threats

session1.details: Study the Checks-Captures-Threats method for scanning any position before moving

session2.details: Solve 15 puzzles requiring 2-3 move calculation, writing down the line before moving

session3.details: Calculate a short 2-move combination in your head before touching the board, then verify

session4.details: Play 2 games applying CCT scanning before every move, especially before opponent's reply

weeklyGoals: Apply the CCT method automatically before every candidate move
Correctly calculate 2-3 move tactical sequences without moving pieces first
Reduce one-move blunders (hanging pieces) to near zero in practice games
Solve 60+ calculation puzzles this month at 75%+ accuracy

months.title: Year 1 Review & First Tournament
months.focus: Consolidate Year 1 material, assess rating progress, and play a first real tournament

session1.details: Revisit weak spots from Months 1-11 using the glossary and reference sections

session2.details: Solve 20 mixed puzzles covering all tactical motifs learned this year

session3.details: Play 2-4 rated games (online or OTB) with a real clock and record every game

session4.details: Analyse one tournament game in full: opening, key moment, and the decisive mistake

weeklyGoals: Score at least 50% in a real tournament or rated game session
Correctly name every tactical pattern learned this year from a diagram
Complete a full self-analysis of a tournament game without engine help first
Set a concrete rating and study goal for Year 2
resources: A local or online beginner tournament

year2.title: Year 2: Skill Development
year2.description: Deepen tactical skills, expand opening knowledge, master positional play

months.title: Intermediate Tactics — Combinations
months.focus: Multi-move combinations that chain 2+ tactical motifs together

session1.details: Study how combinations link forks, pins, and deflections into a forced sequence

session2.details: Solve 15 puzzles rated 1200-1500 requiring 3+ move combinations

session3.details: Study 2 classic sacrificial combinations (e.g., Greek Gift, exchange sacrifice) move by move

session4.details: Play 2 games actively hunting for tactical opportunities rather than waiting for mistakes

weeklyGoals: Solve 3-move combination puzzles at 70%+ accuracy
Correctly evaluate whether a sacrifice is sound before playing it
Successfully execute a multi-move combination in a real or training game
Explain the Greek Gift sacrifice conditions from memory

months.title: Opening Repertoire Deepening
months.focus: Extending your repertoire into main theoretical lines and typical plans

session1.details: Deepen your White opening to move 12-15, including one critical sideline

session2.details: Extend your Black defence vs 1.e4 with typical middlegame plans

session3.details: Extend your Black defence vs 1.d4, including move-order tricks

session4.details: Play games and check post-game whether you followed prepared theory correctly

weeklyGoals: Reach a known, comfortable middlegame in 80%+ of your games
Handle at least 2 common sidelines/deviations for each opening
Understand the typical pawn breaks and piece placement for your repertoire
Build a written repertoire document (moves + key ideas) for future review
resources: Chessable repertoire course matching your openings
ChessBase/lichess study for personal repertoire notes

months.title: Positional Play — Piece Activity & Imbalances
months.focus: Evaluating positions by piece activity, space, and structural imbalances

session1.details: Study the imbalance checklist: material, pawn structure, piece activity, space, king safety

session2.details: Replay 2 classic positional games (Karpov or Petrosian) with light annotation

session3.details: Assess 10 middlegame diagrams using the imbalance checklist and pick a plan

session4.details: Play 2 games where you write down your plan after move 10 and check if you followed it

weeklyGoals: Correctly assess a middlegame position across all 6 imbalance categories
Formulate a concrete multi-move plan in the middlegame, not just single moves
Identify piece activity differences and know how to improve your worst piece
Successfully execute a stated pre-move plan in at least one practice game
resources: Silman's How to Reassess Your Chess

months.title: Middlegame Planning
months.focus: Turning positional assessment into concrete plans: pawn breaks, piece regrouping, attacks

session1.details: Study typical middlegame plans for your repertoire's pawn structures (IQP, hanging pawns, etc.)

session2.details: Replay 2 games showing a textbook minority attack or kingside pawn storm

session3.details: Solve 10 'find the plan' exercises (not tactics — strategic decision puzzles)

session4.details: Play 2 games consciously picking one long-term plan per game and sticking to it

weeklyGoals: Identify at least 3 common middlegame pawn structures and their typical plans
Execute a minority attack or pawn storm plan in a training game
Distinguish between a position needing a tactical solution vs a strategic plan
Reduce 'planless' or drifting moves in your own games

months.title: Minor Piece Endgames
months.focus: Bishop vs knight endgames, same-coloured and opposite-coloured bishop endings

session1.details: Study when bishops are better than knights and vice versa

session2.details: Study opposite-coloured bishop endgame drawing tendencies and how to press for a win

session3.details: Solve 15 minor-piece endgame puzzles

session4.details: Play training games from bishop vs knight endgame starting positions

weeklyGoals: Explain when a bishop is favoured over a knight in an endgame (open position, both wings)
Correctly judge whether an opposite-bishop endgame is drawn or winning
Convert a won bishop vs knight endgame in a training game
Recognise 'good bishop vs bad bishop' structures
resources: 100 Endgames You Must Know — minor piece chapters

months.title: Advanced Rook Endgames
months.focus: Rook endgames beyond Lucena/Philidor: 4th-rank cutoffs, connected passed pawns, and rook activity

session1.details: Study rook + 2 pawns vs rook, and the importance of rook activity behind passed pawns

session2.details: Study the Vancura position for defending against a rook pawn

session3.details: Solve 15 advanced rook endgame puzzles

session4.details: Play training games from complex rook + pawns endgame positions

weeklyGoals: Correctly apply the Vancura defence in a rook pawn endgame
Prioritise rook activity over pawn-grabbing in practice games
Convert a rook + extra pawn endgame to a win at 70%+ success rate
Recognise when to trade into a won pawn endgame from a rook endgame
resources: Dvoretsky's Endgame Manual — rook endgame chapters

months.title: Attacking the King
months.focus: Building and executing attacks against a castled king, including sacrificial breakthroughs

session1.details: Study classic attacking patterns: opening the h-file, Greek Gift, piece storms

session2.details: Replay 2 famous attacking games (Kasparov, Tal) with annotation on key attacking decisions

session3.details: Solve 15 puzzles themed around king attacks and sacrifices

session4.details: Play 2 games in sharp openings, prioritising attacking chances over material

weeklyGoals: Recognise when a king-side attack is objectively justified vs unsound
Correctly calculate a forced sacrificial attack at least 4 moves deep
Execute a successful attacking plan (not just a random sacrifice) in a training game
Study and explain one Tal or Kasparov attacking masterpiece in full
resources: The Art of Attack in Chess (Vladimir Vukovic)
My 60 Memorable Games (Bobby Fischer) — attacking games

months.title: Defense Techniques
months.focus: Defending difficult positions: prophylaxis, exchanging attackers, and finding only-moves

session1.details: Study prophylactic thinking — 'what does my opponent want to do?' before every move

session2.details: Replay 2 famous defensive games (Petrosian, Karpov) surviving an attack

session3.details: Solve 15 'find the only move' or 'save the position' defensive puzzles

session4.details: Play 2 training games from a worse/defensive position (set up by coach or engine) and try to hold

weeklyGoals: Apply prophylactic thinking before at least one move per game
Correctly identify forced-only moves in defensive puzzle positions
Successfully defend and hold a worse position to a draw in a training game
Explain the difference between active and passive defence, with an example of each

months.title: Pawn Structures — IQP & Hanging Pawns
months.focus: Deep dive into the isolated queen's pawn and hanging pawns structures

session1.details: Study the isolated queen's pawn: dynamic play for the side with it, blockade for the side against it

session2.details: Study hanging pawns structures and their attacking/defending strategies

session3.details: Replay 2 annotated games featuring IQP or hanging pawns middlegames

session4.details: Play 2 games from your repertoire that typically lead to an IQP or hanging pawns structure

weeklyGoals: Explain the trade-offs (dynamic activity vs long-term weakness) of the IQP
Correctly choose between attacking or blockading an IQP depending on which side you're on
Identify hanging pawns structures and their typical break (...c4 or ...d4)
Play one complete game demonstrating correct IQP strategy from either side

months.title: Calculation & Visualization Training
months.focus: Deepening calculation depth and board visualization without moving pieces

session1.details: Solve 10 puzzles by calculating fully in your head before moving any piece

session2.details: Practice selecting 2-4 candidate moves and calculating each to a concrete conclusion

session3.details: Solve 15 puzzles requiring 4+ move calculation

session4.details: Play 2 slower games (30+ min) forcing yourself to calculate before every non-trivial move

weeklyGoals: Calculate 3-4 move forcing lines accurately without moving pieces
Use the candidate-moves method consistently instead of calculating one line at a time
Solve 60+ calculation-heavy puzzles this month at 70%+ accuracy
Reduce calculation errors (miscounting material, missing intermezzos) in practice games
resources: Calculate Like a Grandmaster resources (various authors)

months.title: Opening Repertoire vs Sidelines
months.focus: Preparing for the tricky sidelines and gambits opponents use against your repertoire

session1.details: Study the 2-3 most common sidelines opponents play against your White opening

session2.details: Study anti-theory tries and gambits opponents use against your Black defence to 1.e4

session3.details: Study sidelines and move-order tricks against your Black defence to 1.d4

session4.details: Play games specifically inviting sidelines to test your preparation

weeklyGoals: Have a prepared response to the 3 most common sidelines for each opening
Avoid being surprised by a common gambit or trap in your repertoire this month
Update your written repertoire notes with sideline responses
Win or hold at least 2 games where an opponent deviated from main theory
resources: Lichess Opening Explorer (filter by rating band)

months.title: Year 2 Review & Tournament Cycle
months.focus: Consolidate Year 2 material, analyse a full tournament, and set Year 3 goals

session1.details: Revisit weak spots from Months 13-23 using glossary, curriculum and reference sections

session2.details: Solve 20 mixed puzzles rated 1300-1600 covering tactics, endgames, and calculation

session3.details: Play a multi-round rated tournament (4+ games) with full time control

session4.details: Analyse two tournament games in full, including engine comparison after your own analysis

weeklyGoals: Score at least 50% against opponents rated 1400-1600
Correctly self-diagnose the cause of any loss (opening, tactic, endgame, or time trouble)
Complete a written post-mortem for every tournament game
Set a concrete rating and specific weak-area goal for Year 3
resources: A weekend swiss tournament or long online arena

year3.title: Year 3: Advanced Mastery
year3.description: Reach strong club player level with comprehensive chess understanding

months.title: Advanced Tactics — Quiet Moves & Zwischenzug
months.focus: Non-forcing tactical resources: quiet moves, in-between moves, and prophylactic tactics

session1.details: Study 'quiet move' combinations and the zwischenzug (in-between move)

session2.details: Solve 15 puzzles rated 1600-1900 that require a non-capturing, non-checking key move

session3.details: Replay 2 games featuring a decisive zwischenzug or quiet prophylactic move

session4.details: Play 2 games consciously looking for quiet strengthening moves before forcing lines

weeklyGoals: Solve 'quiet move' puzzles at 65%+ accuracy
Correctly identify a zwischenzug opportunity in a live game
Play at least one strong quiet/prophylactic move that a lower-rated player would miss
Explain why forcing moves aren't always the strongest move in a position

months.title: Strategic Masterpieces
months.focus: Deep study of classical strategic games to internalise long-term planning

session1.details: Study one classical strategic game in full depth (Capablanca, Rubinstein, Karpov)

session2.details: Write your own annotations for a game before checking a master's annotations

session3.details: Solve 10 strategic decision puzzles (choosing the best plan, not the best tactic)

session4.details: Play 2 games trying to emulate the strategic theme studied that week

weeklyGoals: Fully annotate one classic game with plans, not just move evaluations
Identify the strategic theme (e.g., minority attack, good knight vs bad bishop) in 5 different games
Apply a studied strategic theme successfully in a training game
Build a personal collection of 10 annotated model games by month's end

months.title: Complex Endgames — Queen & Opposite Bishops
months.focus: Queen endgames, opposite-coloured bishops with other pieces, and complex technique

session1.details: Study queen vs queen endgames: perpetual check avoidance, king safety, technique

session2.details: Study queen vs pawn (especially rook-pawn/bishop-pawn) theoretical positions

session3.details: Solve 15 advanced queen and opposite-bishop endgame puzzles

session4.details: Play training games from complex queen endgame starting positions

weeklyGoals: Correctly convert a queen vs pawn endgame in the winning cases
Avoid perpetual check when ahead in a queen endgame at 80%+ success rate
Judge attacking chances vs drawing tendencies in opposite-bishop middlegames with rooks/queens
Solve 60+ advanced endgame puzzles this month at 65%+ accuracy
resources: Dvoretsky's Endgame Manual — queen endgame chapters
100 Endgames You Must Know — advanced chapters

months.title: Opening Theory Deep Dive
months.focus: Going deeper into critical, forcing lines of your main repertoire with engine-checked accuracy

session1.details: Study the most theoretically critical, forcing line in your main White opening to move 18-20

session2.details: Study the most critical line in your main Black defence to move 15-18

session3.details: Review recent high-level games in your repertoire lines for new ideas or improvements

session4.details: Play games specifically steering into your most-prepared critical lines

weeklyGoals: Play your most critical repertoire line from memory to move 15+
Understand the resulting typical endgame or middlegame structure, not just the moves
Identify at least one recent grandmaster game relevant to your repertoire
Update repertoire notes with critical-line analysis and key evaluation

months.title: Dynamic vs Static Advantages
months.focus: Understanding when to favour piece activity/initiative over long-term structural factors

session1.details: Study the concept of compensation: sacrificing material/structure for activity or initiative

session2.details: Replay 2 games where a player sacrificed a pawn or exchange for lasting dynamic compensation

session3.details: Solve 10 'is this compensation sufficient?' evaluation exercises

session4.details: Play 2 games willing to accept a slightly worse structure for more active piece play

weeklyGoals: Correctly judge whether a pawn sacrifice gives sufficient compensation
Successfully play a position with lasting initiative despite a material deficit
Explain the difference between permanent (static) and temporary (dynamic) advantages
Identify 3 historical examples of a 'positional exchange sacrifice'
resources: Chess Strategy for Club Players (Herman Grooten)

months.title: Exchange & Positional Sacrifices
months.focus: Recognising and executing the exchange sacrifice and other long-term positional sacrifices

session1.details: Study classic exchange sacrifices (rook for knight/bishop) for structure, colour complex, or initiative

session2.details: Replay 2-3 famous exchange-sacrifice games (Petrosian is a model here)

session3.details: Solve 10 puzzles/positions asking 'should Black/White sacrifice the exchange here?'

session4.details: Play 2 games looking specifically for a sound exchange sacrifice opportunity

weeklyGoals: Correctly evaluate when an exchange sacrifice yields long-term compensation
Execute one sound exchange sacrifice in a training game
List the typical justifications for an exchange sacrifice (bad bishop, weak colour complex, strong knight)
Explain why Petrosian is considered a model for this technique

months.title: Advanced Calculation — Candidate Moves
months.focus: Refining the candidate-moves method for complex, non-forcing middlegame positions

session1.details: Practice generating 3-5 candidate moves in quiet (non-tactical) middlegame positions

session2.details: Calculate 5+ move lines fully in your head for 8 complex positions

session3.details: Solve 15 puzzles rated 1900+ combining calculation and evaluation

session4.details: Play 2 slower games (45+ min) applying the full candidate-moves process each critical moment

weeklyGoals: Consistently generate 3+ candidate moves before deciding, even in quiet positions
Calculate accurately to 5+ moves in complex positions without moving pieces
Solve 60+ advanced puzzles this month at 60%+ accuracy
Reduce time-trouble blunders by applying structured calculation earlier in the game

months.title: Time Management & Tournament Psychology
months.focus: Practical skills for clock management, focus, and emotional control in serious games

session1.details: Study clock allocation strategies for different time controls and how to avoid time trouble

session2.details: Study tilt recovery, pre-game routines, and focus techniques used by strong players

session3.details: Play 2 full-length rated games under real tournament time control conditions

session4.details: Journal about emotional state, time usage, and focus lapses after each game

weeklyGoals: Finish games with at least 5 minutes on the clock in 80%+ of practice games
Identify personal tilt triggers and apply one recovery technique after a bad result
Maintain a consistent pre-game routine before every practice/tournament game
Keep a written log of time usage and psychological notes for at least 8 games

months.title: Complete Repertoire Consolidation
months.focus: Building a fully connected, tournament-ready opening repertoire for White and Black

session1.details: Review your entire White repertoire tree for gaps and update weak branches

session2.details: Review and finalise your Black repertoire against 1.e4 including rare tries

session3.details: Review and finalise your Black repertoire against 1.d4 and flank openings (1.c4, 1.Nf3)

session4.details: Play a mix of games testing every branch of your repertoire against varied opponents

weeklyGoals: Have a prepared, memorised response to every opening a typical opponent might play
Identify and close the 3 biggest remaining gaps in your repertoire
Produce a complete, organised repertoire document/study for future reference
Play 5+ consecutive games without being taken out of prepared theory

months.title: Advanced Endgame Technique
months.focus: Fortresses, zugzwang, and technical conversion of small advantages

session1.details: Study fortress positions where the defender holds despite material deficit

session2.details: Study zugzwang in king and pawn, and minor piece endgames

session3.details: Solve 15 puzzles on converting a small advantage (extra pawn, better minor piece)

session4.details: Play training games from a small-but-real endgame advantage and practice converting it

weeklyGoals: Recognise a fortress position and hold a draw as the defender
Correctly identify and exploit a zugzwang opportunity
Convert a small endgame advantage to a full point at 60%+ success rate in training games
Explain the difference between a 'technically winning' and 'practically difficult' endgame
resources: Dvoretsky's Endgame Manual — fortress and zugzwang chapters
100 Endgames You Must Know — advanced set

months.title: Tournament Preparation & Opponent Prep
months.focus: Practical preparation: researching opponents, adapting strategy, and simulating tournament conditions

session1.details: Practice looking up a hypothetical opponent's games/repertoire and preparing a plan against it

session2.details: Prepare a specific line tailored to counter a known opponent tendency

session3.details: Play a full rated game simulating real tournament conditions (arrive early, full focus, no distractions)

session4.details: Debrief the simulated round: opening choice, time usage, psychological state, and result

weeklyGoals: Successfully prepare a targeted opening line against a specific opponent profile
Apply opponent research to gain a practical advantage in at least one simulated game
Maintain full tournament-standard focus and routine across a simulated round
Produce a complete pre-round preparation checklist for future tournaments

months.title: Final Review, Mastery Assessment & Beyond
months.focus: Consolidate all 3 years, assess readiness for 1800-2000 level play, and plan continued growth

session1.details: Revisit key concepts across all 3 years using curriculum, glossary, and reference sections

session2.details: Solve 25 mixed puzzles spanning tactics, strategy, and endgames at your target rating

session3.details: Play a multi-round rated tournament as a capstone assessment of 3 years of study

session4.details: Review your 10 best and 10 worst games from the past year to identify remaining weaknesses

weeklyGoals: Achieve or approach the 1800-2000 rating target set at the start of the plan
Correctly self-diagnose remaining weak areas (e.g., specific endgame type, time trouble, opening gaps)
Produce a personal 'Year 4+' study plan targeting identified weaknesses
Complete a full annotated portfolio of 20 personal games with lessons learned
resources: In-app full curriculum and glossary for final review
A rated tournament (OTB or online) as capstone
Personal 'lessons learned' journal from the full 3-year plan

sessions.details: Study one chess concept from curriculum
Play 2-3 games focusing on learned concept
Deep dive into specific opening lines
Play practice games with time control
Enjoy and learn from master games
